candidates.title: Check public claims before buying a startup tool

demandEvidence.chore: A prospective business software buyer wants to judge whether a product’s customer-base claims are credible.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: So as someone looking to buy a YC product, I'm not sure if I'm being hustled or if they actually have a good customer base.

ease.reason: A beginner could compare a public product page with a short checklist, but no research method or implementation source is supplied.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent business software buyers may pay for a credibility brief; this post does not prove demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can organize operator-supplied public claims and links; source access and reliable verification remain untested.

autonomy.reason: The tool could organize claims, but a person must inspect sources and judge whether customer evidence is credible.

evidence.reason: The post states uncertainty about a YC product’s customer base, but names no product, claim or repeated research process.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (mean 4.2). A public-claim checklist is a possible experiment, but the excerpt is too broad to support a more specific research workflow; no post proposed.

candidates.title: Turn invoice emails into reviewable rows

demandEvidence.chore: Bookkeepers and small finance teams manually retype vendor invoice details from email into a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: still retype vendor invoices from email into a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A beginner can test extraction on fictional invoice examples, but no supplied implementation reference supports email or spreadsheet connections.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bookkeepers or small finance teams may pay to reduce invoice retyping; the post establishes no AI-service payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can turn operator-supplied sample invoice text into proposed rows; formats and live integrations remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Extraction can prepare rows repeatedly, while a bookkeeper must verify amounts, identifiers and any tax checks before entry.

evidence.reason: The post directly identifies bookkeepers retyping emailed vendor invoices into a spreadsheet, but gives no volume or field details.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (mean 4.6). The concrete retyping chore supports a mock extraction experiment, but no implementation reference supports integrations and a human must verify every row; no post proposed.
